title: A Echo for the Orbit
premise: On the terraforming moon Verity, Ada Dunmore is the last caretaker of a seed-vault garden meant for colonists still in cryosleep, recording daily logs of a dying ecosystem no one will ever hear. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew biologically aged backward into children, Ada discovers the truth: the colony's founders rigged the cryo-systems to wake only half of humanity, sacrificing the rest to keep Verity alive. As the regressed crew's fragmented adult memories surface, Ada must choose between waking her own forgotten generation or preserving the children who are the colony's only future. In the end, Ada merges both archives—her garden's memory and the crew's restored recollections—and wakes a third, unrecorded group hidden by the founders, ensuring neither half of humanity is erased.
about_author: I. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former botanical archivist who spent six years cataloguing seed banks in remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who tend things no one else remembers exist.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She tends the failing greenhouse on Verity, recording log entries for colonists she believes will never wake, mourning a colleague who abandoned the post years ago. The emotional beat is quiet devotion shadowed by futility—she gardens anyway, because someone must remember what was promised.

chapters.title: A Ship Out of Yesterday
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Halcyon descends unannounced after forty years; its crew emerges as children wearing adults' memories like ill-fitting clothes. Ada recognizes the mission commander, now eight years old, as the woman who signed the order abandoning the surface. The beat is uncanny wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: Commander Reyes-Okonkwo's POV, fractured and childlike. The regressed crew struggles with memories that don't fit their bodies, including fragments of a decision made in deep space: half the cryopods were flagged to never open. The beat is disorientation and guilt too large for small hands.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decrypting the colony archive, she finds the founders' covenant: Verity can sustain either the ten thousand sleepers or the terraformed biosphere, not both. Her own name appears on the list of those to be sacrificed. The beat is cold betrayal—the garden was always a grave marker.

chapters.title: What the Roots Remember
chapters.summary: Reyes-Okonkwo's POV. The child-commander leads her crew to a buried founder's vault beneath Ada's greenhouse, where genetic records reveal the 'backward aging' was engineered—a failsafe to preserve decision-makers past their own corruption. The beat is horrified recognition that they were made into instruments.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Breath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ada argues for waking all the sleepers even if the biosphere collapses; the child-crew argues the children themselves are the future worth saving. Their alliance fractures when Ada learns Reyes-Okonkwo cast the original sacrifice vote. The beat is righteous anger meeting desperate self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Verity
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Life-support systems begin cascading failure; the choice can no longer be deferred. Ada broadcasts her decades of logs colony-wide, forcing every faction to confront the accumulated cost of forgetting. The beat is grief transformed into testimony—memory as an act of power.

chapters.title: Climax: The Vote in the Vault
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge in the founder's vault. With hours remaining, Ada proposes a third option hinted in corrupted files: an unlisted pod bay the founders hid from themselves. Reyes-Okonkwo, using her regressed state as proof the system corrupts everyone, overrides the covenant. The beat is defiant hope against certain ruin.

chapters.title: Waking the Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Reyes-Okonkwo's POV. The hidden bay opens: descendants of the founders' own exiled dissenters, ten thousand strong, never entered in any ledger. As they wake, Ada's garden becomes a nursery rather than a memorial. The beat is trembling reconciliation—identity rebuilt from what was deliberately erased.

chapters.title: An Echo for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, final log entry. Years later, Verity holds both the woken dissenters and the slowly re-aging crew, governed by an archive no one may edit. Ada plants the last seed row and addresses it to whoever comes next. The beat is earned peace: power held accountable, memory kept alive, identity chosen rather than assigned.
